In the event that a Zoom broadcast is unavailable, staff will promptly notify the public through its social media platforms. The public
meeting will proceed in accordance with the Brown Act.

Spontaneous Communications: The public is encouraged to address the Parks & Recreation Commission on any matter listed on the
agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments on items listed
on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Parks & Recreation Commission will hear public comments on
matters not listed on the agenda during the Spontaneous Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The Parks & Recreation Commission may request from staff to investigate and/or schedule
certain matters for consideration at a future Commission or City Council meeting.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA and Government Code section 54953(g), the City Council has adopted a
reasonable accommodation policy to swiftly resolve accommodation requests. The policy can be found on the City’s website:
https://www.irwindaleca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/8075/AB-2449-Reasonable-Accommodation-Policy. If you need special
assistance to participate in a City Council or Commission meeting or other services offered by this City, including an electronic or
printed copy of the City’s reasonable accommodation policy, please contact City Hall at (626) 430-2200. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the city staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be
made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Staff reports are available for inspection by appointment only at the office of the City Clerk, City Hall, 5050 N. Irwindale Avenue,
during regular business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday)

  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality and
integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain from
abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which we
have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create a
perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest in
thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

CONSENT CALENDAR
The Consent Calendar contains matters of routine business and is to be approved with one motion unless a member of
the Commission requests separate action on a specific item. At this time, members of the audience may ask to be heard
regarding an item on the Consent Calendar.

  1. Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the following minutes:

  A. Regular meeting held October 4, 2023.

SPONTANEOUS COMMUNICATIONS
This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits any
Commission discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds that a
catastrophe or emergency exists; or 2) the Commission by at least four votes finds that the matter (and need for action
thereon) arose within the last five days. Since the Commission cannot (except as stated) participate, it is requested that
all such communications be made in writing so as to be included on the next agenda for full discussion and action. If a
member of the audience feels he or she must proceed tonight, then each speaker will be limited to 3 minutes unless such
time limits are extended.

Any public member addressing the Board shall limit his or her address to three (3) minutes regarding the subject
under discussion. If a member of the public wishes to donate their time to another speaker, both persons must
be physically present and in attendance of the meeting. In no event shall any donations of time exceed six minutes
of total speaking time per person on any one item. The Presiding Officer may, in his or her discretion, extend the
3-minute time limitation for the particular subject under discussion for all speakers. In no event shall the total
amount of speaking time exceed 6 minutes per person for the subject under discussion. Organized group of
persons wishing to address the Board on the same subject matter, should select a spokesperson to represent the
group, so as to avoid unnecessary repetition. The Commission may regulate a speaker who is speaking too long,
being unduly repetitious, or extending discussion of irrelevancies.

Public Comments will be heard in the following order:

1 – Email comments

2 – In-person attendees

and place.

ITEM NO. 1  MINUTES
MINUTES
  The following minutes were approved as presented:

  1) Regular meeting held September 6, 2023.

SPONTANEOUS
COMMUNICATIONS  There were no speakers.

RECREATION
MANAGER UPDATE

RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda provided the following update:
MANAGER ZEPEDA
  1) She has reached out to the president of the San Gabriel Valley
  LGBTQ chapter to discuss ideas for an event that Irwindale could
  participate in but has yet to hear back.
  2) The Teen Club has a Board, complete with a President, Giovanni
  Salgado.
  3) She thanked staff from all departments for their hard work in
  organizing the MariachiFest concerts in September.
  4) Twenty participants joined in a soccer clinic with SoFive Soccer
  Center last month. Staff also discussed staff’s efforts in
  disseminating information regarding the clinic.
  5) She also provided the dates for upcoming events and activities.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  OCTOBER 4, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 2

  6) She recognized Recreation Aide Alan Hernandez for being
  selected as the Recreation Department’s Employee of the
  Quarter.
  7) She also noted that this is Customer Service Week and
  acknowledged members of staff for their roles in providing quality
  customer service to the public.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez noted that the commission previously consented
  in organizing a trip in recognition of Pride Month, to which Chair
  Fraijo stated that staff could let the community know about such a
  trip so that those who would like to participate may do so.

AQUATICS
SUPERVISOR UPDATE

AQUATICS  Aquatics Supervisor Grijalva provided the following update:
SUPERVISOR GRIJALVA
  1) The Recreational Swimming sessions offered during September
  weekends have concluded.
  2) The Aquatics Center fall schedule will run from October 2
  through November 2.
  3) He provided the details on scheduled sessions of Mindful
  Waters, Senior Splash/Aqua Walk & Lap Swimming, Aqua Stand
  Up & Aqua Fitness, and Swim Team.
  4) He also advised that he will be attending the Annual SCMAF
  Institute conference tomorrow.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo asked for the number of program participants for
  September, which Supervisor Grijalva acknowledged participation
  was a bit lower. Chair Fraijo recommended that a sign be placed on
  the facility windows indicating that weekend swim sessions are
  open, which may drum up more participation.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman thanked staff for having the pool open until
ROMAN  November.

VICE CHAIR ZEPEDA  Vice Chair Zepeda stated that all attendees enjoyed the luau.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo asked how successful the new snack bar has been, to
  which Supervisor Grijalva stated that it is doing well and noted that
  he would inform the Commission next month regarding the snack
  bar’s sales. Chair Fraijo suggested that a sign be placed near the
  gate advertising that the snack bar is open.

PUBLIC WORKS
SUPERVISOR UPDATE
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  OCTOBER 4, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 3

PUBLIC WORKS  Public Works Supervisor Rodriguez presented the following update:
SUPERVISOR
RODRIGUEZ  1) Staff is working on repairing a few irrigation main line leaks.
  2) Staff also repaired exercise equipment at Jardin de Roca Park.
  3) Building maintenance staff is working on the offices for the
  Maintenance and Engineering Departments.
  4) He also thanked staff for their diligence in preparing for recent
  Recreation Department events.
  5) Staff recently attended environmental safety and workplace
  harassment prevention trainings.

COMMISSIONER  Responding to a concern by Commissioner Roman, Supervisor
ROMAN  Rodriguez noted an issue with the timer for the lighting at the park.
  However, staff is arranging for the repair and have made temporary
  fixes so that the park is properly illuminated.

  Commissioner Roman requested that signs be placed warning
  motorists to drive carefully and to be on the lookout for trick-or-
  treaters. She also requested that the windscreens on the fencing that
  enclose the park areas that are under construction be removed since
  the homeless may trespass into the areas.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez recommended against the suggestion and
  advised that the areas are under surveillance by three cameras and
  noted that staff is working closely with the Police Department to
  mitigate any problems.

VICE CHAIR ZEPEDA  In response to a question by Vice Chair Zepeda, Supervisor
  Rodriguez noted that the sprinklers are down momentarily due to the
  water main line leaks. However, the contractor of the park project is
  watering the trees.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Ortiz asked about the availability of restrooms, to
ORTIZ  which Supervisor Rodriguez indicated that trailer restrooms are
  available. Commissioner Ortiz also noted that the grass at El Nido
  Park seems to be dying, to which Supervisor Rodriguez stated that
  he would follow-up on the concern.

CHAIR FRAIJO  In reply to several questions by Chair Fraijo, Supervisor Rodriguez
  advised that: 1) staff is working on fertilizing and placing winter seed
  on the parks’ lawns, 2) the bearings of certain exercise equipment at
  the Skate Park have been repaired, and 3) reported on an incident
  that required the intervention of the Police Department just outside
  the Skate Park.

PUBLIC SERVICES
DIRECTOR UPDATE
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  OCTOBER 4, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 4

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez presented the following update:

  1) All city departments have been invited to participate in the
  upcoming Trunk or Treat event.
  2) She recognized the renaming of a city facility in honor of David
  Fraijo Martinez held on September 23.
  3) Athens Services, in collaboration with the City, will host a bulky
  item pickup event on October 13.
  4) Athens is providing free compost during a giveaway event to be
  held on October 14.
  5) She provided an update on the Irwindale Park Improvement
  Project and noted that staff has requested that the contractor set
  up temporary lighting in the area.
  6) She also thanked all that attended the recent city-facility renaming
  event honoring David Fraijo Martinez.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo expressed concern over wheelchair access along the
  sidewalks near the park construction area, to which Director
  Rodriguez noted that she would speak to Engineering staff as well as
  the contractor to determine how to best provide access.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez also encouraged participating in the City’s Pledge
  Leader program.

COMMISSIONER
COMMENTS AND
FUTURE DISCUSSION
REQUESTS

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman requested that social media posts include
ROMAN  additional details relating to programs and events, such as the dates
  and times that individuals may sign up. She also suggested that the
  next MariachiFest concert series end on September 16 with a
  western-themed concert held the following week.

COMMISSIONER  Responding to a question by Commissioner Ortiz, Manager Zepeda
ORTIZ  advised that detailed information regarding all Recreation programs
  and activities are included in the city website.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Duran expressed her preference for the MariachiFest
DURAN  concerts to be held on Fridays since Thursdays are school nights
  and many are unable to attend. She also noted issues with homeless
  individuals at the bus stop across the street.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman asked whether the bus stop could be fenced
ROMAN  off.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  OCTOBER 4, 2023
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 5

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez advised that staff has discussed replacing the
  existing bus stop with a smaller one and indicated that the project
  would be considered under next year’s budget. She also stated that
  the current bus stop could not be fenced off since it is an active site
  for Foothill Transit.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo requested that the Commission review the rental policy
  at the next meeting and asked that staff look into any open space
  available within the city for the potential development of a designated
  football field, with the results to be presented to the Commission.

  Responding to a concern by Chair Fraijo, Manager Zepeda advised
  that staff has included verbiage in Spanish on program flyers with a
  phone number that could be dialed for additional information in
  Spanish.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez added that the Aquatics and Senior Center flyers
  include the same verbiage.

ADJOURNMENT  There being no further business to conduct, the meeting was
  adjourned at 7:04 p.m. in memory of Richard Herrera.
